name: Namibian Kapana
description: Kapana, Namibia's beloved street-food grilled meat, is real seasoned with a specific spice blend of cumin, coriander, paprika, and thyme, then chopped right on the grill and eaten by hand with a spicy tomato-onion relish - real technique keeps the beef in strips grilled hot and fast over an open flame, chopped into bite-size pieces as it cooks, not before.
steps_detailed: Mix the cumin, coriander, paprika, and thyme, and rub over the beef strips.
Grill the beef strips over high heat, turning, until well charred, 6-8 minutes.
Chop the grilled beef into bite-size pieces right on the grill or a cutting board.
Mix the tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, and vinegar into a fresh relish, and serve alongside the chopped meat to eat by hand.

name: Namibian Oshifima with Ombidi
description: Oshifima, a stiff porridge traditionally made from mahangu (pearl millet), is served with ombidi, a spinach and tomato stew - real mahangu isn't a distinct item here, so cornmeal and real sorghum flour stand in for a similar texture, and real technique beats the flour in gradually to build a dense, dough-like consistency.
steps_detailed: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal and sorghum flour with the salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Gradually beat in the remaining flour, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, until very thick and dough-like.
Meanwhile, cook the onion 3-4 minutes, then add the tomatoes and spinach, and simmer 12-15 minutes.
Serve the oshifima alongside the ombidi.

name: Namibian Potjiekos
description: Potjiekos, meat and vegetables slow-cooked in a round cast-iron pot, reflects genuine Dutch-Afrikaner influence shared with South Africa - real technique layers ingredients without stirring, letting each layer cook in the steam and juices of the one below.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Layer the carrot and potato on top without stirring, add the broth.
Cover and simmer very gently, without stirring, 45-50 minutes, until everything is tender - real potjiekos depends on this undisturbed layering.

name: Namibian Marathon Chicken
description: Marathon chicken, named for the free-range 'hard body' chickens tough enough to earn the nickname, is genuinely cooked in a specific order - real technique boils the chicken first, seasoned simply with just salt, until tender, THEN sears it in marula oil afterward, not browned at the start; the finishing sauce stays deliberately thin and simple, just tomato and onion, without extra herbs or vegetables. Marula oil isn't a distinct item here, so olive oil stands in, missing its real distinctive nutty, fruity finish.

ingredients.note: tbsp, standing in for marula oil

steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken with the salt and just enough water to not quite cover, 30-35 minutes, until the water reduces and the chicken is genuinely tender - real technique starts here, not with browning.
Sear the boiled chicken in the olive oil until golden on all sides, 6-8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and onion, keeping the sauce thin and simple, and simmer 10-12 minutes more.

name: Namibian Fat Cakes (Vetkoek)
description: Sweet Namibian fat cakes, fried dough shared with South Africa, real versions served as a main course for lunch or dinner, not just breakfast.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, baking powder, and sugar with warm water into a soft dough.
Let rest 15 minutes.
Shape into small balls and fry, turning, 4-5 minutes per batch, until deeply golden.

name: Namibian Herero Bread
description: Herero bread, a dense, hearty bread, is a genuine point of pride during Namibian heritage celebrations, real technique baking low and slow for a thick, substantial crust.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, and softened butter with enough water to form a firm dough.
Shape into a round loaf and bake at 350F (175C) for 30-35 minutes until the crust is deeply golden and firm.

name: Namibian Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Namibia's Atlantic coastal fishing tradition, especially around Walvis Bay.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Namibian Milk Tart
description: Melktert, a real custard tart with a cinnamon-dusted top, shared with South Africa, a beloved dessert.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and butter with a little cold water into a firm dough, press into a tart pan, and bake at 375F (190C) for 12-15 minutes.
Whisk the milk, egg, and sugar together and pour into the baked crust.
Bake 20-22 minutes more until just set.
Dust generously with cinnamon once cooled.

name: Namibian Tomato Onion Relish
description: A simple tomato-onion relish, a common Namibian condiment alongside oshifima or grilled meat.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 12-15 minutes until thickened.
